rows.description_html:
Today, we're testing your endurance and mental fortitude with an EMOM challenge that scales in intensity. This workout demands consistent effort and smart pacing to succeed.

Focus on maintaining good form even as fatigue sets in. Every minute counts.
rows.instructions_html:
For the Main Workout, perform the prescribed repetitions of each exercise at the top of every minute. Use the remainder of the minute to rest before the next minute's exercise begins. If you cannot complete the reps within the minute, scale down the reps or take a brief break, then rejoin at the top of the next minute.

For the Finisher, perform as many rounds and repetitions of the given circuit as possible in 5 continuous minutes. Keep track of your rounds and reps.

rows.name: Trial Cascade
rows.tips_html:
Pacing is critical in an EMOM. Find a rhythm that allows you to complete the reps and still get 15-20 seconds of rest before the next minute.

Maintain impeccable form throughout. As fatigue mounts, resist the urge to sacrifice movement quality for speed. Good technique prevents injury and ensures proper muscle engagement.

Scale exercises or reps as needed. If 10 burpees is too much in a minute, reduce it to 7 or 8. The goal is continuous work, not failure.

For the Finisher, break up reps early if needed. Small, consistent sets will get you further than going all out and then burning out.

Listen to your body throughout the session; any discomfort beyond a mild stretch or muscle engagement should prompt you to reduce intensity or stop.

rows.description_html:
This advanced mobility and stability workout, "Grounding Pillar Stability," is meticulously designed to enhance your foundational strength and joint integrity. Utilizing precise, controlled movements with equipment, it targets deep stabilization muscles to improve overall body control and reduce injury risk.

Expect a challenging session focused on slow tempos and extensive ranges of motion, perfect for those ready to master their body's inherent stability mechanisms.
rows.instructions_html:
Warm-Up: Begin with light cardio to elevate your heart rate. Follow with dynamic movements like Cat-Cow and Thread the Needle to prepare your spine and shoulders. Bird-Dogs activate core stability.

Main Workout (Pillar Forge): This section focuses on controlled, advanced stability movements. For the Single-Arm Kettlebell Overhead Carry, choose a weight that allows you to maintain perfect posture without leaning. The Goblet Squat with Bottom Hold emphasizes time under tension and hip mobility. Turkish Get-Ups require extreme focus on segmental control – prioritize form over speed. The Pallof Press is an anti-rotation exercise; resist the band's pull. Finish with Single-Leg RDLs, maintaining a stable hip throughout. Rest periods are crucial for recovery and maintaining form.

Finisher (Core Control Flow): Conclude with a plank circuit, focusing on sustained core engagement. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels during all plank variations.

Cool-Down: Use static stretches to improve flexibility and aid recovery. Focus on deep breathing and relaxing into each stretch.

rows.name: Grounding Pillar Stability
rows.tips_html:
Master the Carry: {{exercise:3548:dumbbell single arm overhead carry}}, imagine you are walking on a tightrope while balancing a book on your head. This mental cue will help you maintain an upright posture and engage your deep core stabilizers.

Slow Down to Speed Up: In Mobility & Stability workouts, tempo is your friend. Execute each repetition with deliberate control, focusing on the muscle contraction and maintaining tension throughout the entire range of motion. This mindfulness enhances proprioception and strengthens neural pathways.

Breathe Through It: Conscious breathing is integral to stability. Inhale to prepare for a movement and exhale with effort, engaging your deep core muscles (transverse abdominis) to create a "corset" effect around your spine.

Quality Over Quantity: Especially in advanced movements like the Turkish Get-Up, prioritize perfect form over attempting more repetitions or heavier weights. A flawless repetition provides more benefit and prevents injury than several sloppy ones.

rows.description_html: This advanced EMOM workout is designed to push your metabolic limits and enhance full-body conditioning using only your body weight. Each minute brings a new challenge, demanding focus and intensity to maximize calorie burn and improve endurance.
rows.instructions_html:
This is a 45-minute advanced metabolic workout structured around an Every Minute On the Minute (EMOM) main block, followed by an intense AMRAP finisher.

For the EMOM: At the top of each minute, perform the given exercise for the prescribed reps or duration. Your rest is whatever time is left in that minute. At the start of the next minute, you'll immediately begin the next exercise.

For the Finisher: Complete As Many Rounds As Possible (AMRAP) of the three-exercise circuit within the 10-minute time cap.

Move consistently and prioritize excellent form. The goal is to keep moving with minimal rest to maximize the metabolic effect.

rows.name: Cadence Helix Flow
rows.tips_html:
Pace yourself in the EMOM. The goal is to complete all rounds, not to burn out in the first 10 minutes. Find a challenging but sustainable pace that allows you to maintain form.

This is an advanced workout. If you can't maintain form or complete the reps within the minute, reduce the rep count. For example, scale from 10 Clap Push-ups to 6, or perform a standard Push-up instead. Quality of movement is always the priority.

Focus on diaphragmatic breathing during the cool-down stretches. Deep inhales through the nose and long exhales through the mouth will help lower your heart rate and activate your parasympathetic nervous system for better recovery.

rows.description_html: Prepare to ignite your metabolism and push your body to its limits with this high-intensity, bodyweight metabolic tabata. 2. Understand Tabata Format: Each Tabata exercise involves 20 seconds of maximum effort work followed by 10 seconds of rest. This is one round. You will complete 8 rounds for each exercise, totaling 4 minutes per exercise.

3. {{exercise:1761:hanging oblique knee raise}} After completing 8 rounds of an exercise, you will have a 60-second rest period before moving to the next Tabata block.

4. Maintain Intensity: The key to Tabata is to give 100% effort during the 20-second work intervals. Push yourself!

5. Proper Form Over Speed: While intensity is crucial, never sacrifice proper form for speed. If your form falters, slow down or take a brief pause before resuming.

6. Cool-down and Stretch: Conclude your workout with the static stretches in the cool-down section to improve flexibility and aid recovery.

rows.tips_html:
Master the Pistol Squat: If full single leg squat (pistol) male is challenging, use a counter-balance (holding arms out front) or reduce the depth. Focus on stability through the whole movement.

Pull-up Perfection: Ensure a full range of motion on all pull-ups. If necessary, use assisted variations or resistance bands to achieve the target reps with good form and controlled negatives.

Engage Your Core: Maintain a strong, braced core throughout all exercises, especially during single-leg movements and pull-ups, to protect your spine and transfer power efficiently.

Listen to Your Body: While this is an advanced workout, prioritize quality over quantity. If form breaks down, reduce reps or take a brief pause, then reset.

rows.description_html: Challenge your core and balance with this intermediate mat Pilates workout. Combines classical Pilates exercises with balance challenges to develop a strong, stable center.
rows.instructions_html: Maintain neutral spine unless instructed otherwise. Engage your deep core muscles before each movement. Breathe with intention.
rows.main_workout:
🧽 Soft Tissue Preparation 1'

  • Self-massage — 30 sec total across the outer hips using gentle hand contact; avoid bony points.

  • Self-massage — 30 sec total across the thighs using relaxed palms; keep the sensation comfortable.

🔥 Activation 3'

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1422:pelvic tilt into bridge}} — gently articulate upward over 3 sec and downward over 3 sec; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:0276:Dead Bug}} — alternate short reaches, taking 3 sec outward and 3 sec back; keep breathing comfortably; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:clamshell:Clamshell}} — 15 sec per side, lifting for 2 sec and lowering for 3 sec through a small range; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1363:spine stretch}} — gently lengthen forward for 3 sec and return for 3 sec without forcing range; rest 15 sec.

💪 Main Workout (REPS & SETS)

Complete all sets of each exercise before continuing. Prescribed repetitions and rests total 33 min 7 sec; allow approximately 53 sec overall for position changes, bringing the main workout to 34 min. Include the final prescribed rest on each line. Before the first repetition, settle your ribs over your pelvis and establish relaxed, continuous breathing.

  • 3 sets × 8 reps {{exercise:the-hundred:The Hundred}} — tempo 3-sec controlled lift, 1-sec pause, 3-sec lower, 1-sec reset; rest 45 sec after each set. Exhale as the shoulder blades leave the floor; keep the neck long and avoid pulling the head forward.

  • 2 sets × 10 reps {{exercise:pilates-rolling-like-a-ball:Rolling Like A Ball}} — tempo 3-sec gradual rise, 1-sec pause, 3-sec articulated return, 1-sec reset; rest 45 sec after each set. Reach forward without throwing the arms or using momentum; use only the range you can reverse smoothly.

  • 3 sets × 10 reps {{exercise:pilates-swan-dive:Swan Dive}} — alternate sides for 5 reps per side per set; tempo 2-sec foot lift, 2-sec steady hold, 2-sec foot return; rest 45 sec after each set. Keep the pelvis level and the supporting foot grounded; lower fully during each rest.

  • 2 sets × 10 reps per side {{exercise:pilates-scissors:Scissors}} — tempo 2-sec hip lift, 1-sec pause, 3-sec lower; rest 45 sec after each side, including the final side. Complete both sides to finish one set; stop the lift before the lower back arches.

  • 2 sets × 10 reps per side {{exercise:pilates-leg-pull-back:Leg Pull Back}} — tempo 2-sec hip lift, 1-sec pause, 3-sec controlled lower; rest 45 sec after each side, including the final side. Complete both sides to finish one set; keep the supporting elbow beneath the shoulder and lift without rotating.

  • 3 sets × 10 reps {{exercise:pilates-chest-lift-rotation:Chest Lift With Rotation}} — one rep is one left-leg lift and one right-leg lift; take 3 sec to lift and return each leg, giving 6 sec per rep; rest 45 sec after each set. Keep the movement small, the pelvis quiet and the neck aligned; reach the legs long rather than lifting them high.

🧘 Cool Down 3'

  • 30 sec per side {{exercise:0613:lying (side) quads stretch}} — hold still at mild tension and breathe out into the position; rest 5 sec to change position.

  • 30 sec per side {{exercise:1424:seated glute stretch}} — maintain a comfortable, steady hold and breathe out into the position; rest 5 sec to change position.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1363:spine stretch}} — hold a gentle forward lengthening position without bouncing; breathe out into the position; rest 5 sec.

15 sec relaxed breathing — inhale gently through the nose and let each exhale soften the abdomen and shoulders.

During the main workout, prioritize maintaining proper form and engaging your core throughout each exercise. For lunges, ensure your knee tracks over your toes and your torso remains upright. For single leg deadlifts, keep a slight bend in your standing knee and hinge from the hips, maintaining a flat back.

The finisher should challenge your core endurance and range of motion without sacrificing technique. Move slowly and intentionally.

rows.name: Arcane Weave
rows.tips_html:
Tip 1: Breath Control: Coordinate your breathing with each movement. Inhale during the eccentric (lowering) phase and exhale during the concentric (lifting) phase. This helps brace your core and optimize stability.

Tip 2: Mind-Muscle Connection: Actively think about the muscles you are working. This enhances recruitment and helps you move more efficiently and effectively.

Tip 3: Controlled Tempo: For mobility and stability, rushing through reps diminishes their effectiveness. Aim for a 2-second concentric, 1-second pause at the peak, and a 3-second eccentric phase for most exercises.

Tip 4: Listen to Your Body: If you feel any sharp pain, stop the exercise. Modify exercises as needed to match your current ability and focus on injury prevention.

rows.tips_html:

Breathing Strategy: Consciously control your breathing. Inhale through your nose, exhale powerfully through your mouth to regulate your heart rate and maintain oxygen flow.

Form Over Speed: Especially when fatigued, prioritize perfect form. Sloppy reps negate the benefits and increase injury risk. If form breaks, rest or scale.

Mental Grit: This is a challenge, so expect to feel uncomfortable. Push through the desire to stop, focus on one rep at a time, and remember why you started.

rows.main_workout:
🧽 Soft Tissue Preparation 1'

  • Self-massage calves with your hands — 30 sec total, gentle continuous pressure, 15 sec each side.

  • Self-massage front and outer thighs with your palms — 30 sec total, gentle continuous pressure, 15 sec each side; avoid joints.

🔥 Activation 3'

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1422:pelvic tilt into bridge}} — 1 set; lift gently for 2 sec and lower for 2 sec; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:clamshell:Clamshell}} — 1 set, 15 sec each side; lift and lower slowly through a comfortable range; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1368:Ankle Circles}} — 1 set, 15 sec each side while seated; make slow, comfortable rotations in both directions; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1167:dynamic chest stretch}} — 1 set; open and close the arms gently without bouncing; rest 15 sec.

💪 Main Workout (EMOM)

18 minutes total: 3 rounds of the following 6-minute sequence. Start each station on the minute, work for 35 sec and rest for 25 sec. Each listed station is completed 3 times. Repeated movements deliberately keep the sequence familiar. Maintain an effort of 5–6 out of 10 and the ability to speak a sentence.

  • Minute 1: 35 sec {{exercise:butt-kicks-cardio:Butt Kicks}} — smooth, repeatable pace; use light, relaxed punches into open air, pivot comfortably and return to guard each time; rest 25 sec.

2. Jumping Jack Start with feet together and arms at your sides. Jump, spreading your feet wide and bringing your arms overhead. Jump back to the start. Maintain a steady, controlled pace.

3. High Knees Stand tall and gently march in place, bringing your knees up towards your waist. Focus on controlled movement rather than speed to begin with.

4. {{exercise:3168:bodyweight squatting row}} Stand with feet hip-width apart. Step one foot out to the side, then bring the other foot to meet it. Gradually increase the distance and speed, keeping your chest up. This is a stepping motion, Broad Jump.

5. Cool-down (5 minutes): Finish with gentle static stretches, holding each stretch for 20-30 seconds. Focus on major muscle groups like quads, {{exercise:1511:hamstring stretch}}, standing calves.

rows.description_html: This intermediate, bodyweight-only strength workout targets your core and glutes, building stability and power. Engage your entire trunk and posterior chain for a solid foundation. Perfect for home-friendly training.
rows.instructions_html:
1. Warm-Up: Begin with the prescribed warm-up exercises to prepare your body for movement. Focus on controlled, deliberate movements to increase blood flow and range of motion.

2. Main Workout - Circuit 1: Perform all exercises in Circuit 1 back-to-back with minimal rest between exercises. Once you've completed one round of all four exercises, rest for 60 seconds. Repeat this circuit for a total of 3 rounds.

3. Main Workout - Circuit 2: After completing Circuit 1, move on to Circuit 2. Follow the same structure: perform all exercises back-to-back, rest for 60 seconds after each round, and complete 3 total rounds.

4. Tempo: Pay attention to the tempo listed (e.g., 2010). This means 2 seconds on the eccentric (lowering) phase, 0-second pause at the bottom, 1 second on the concentric (lifting) phase, and 0-second pause at the top. Adjust the tempo to your fitness level, but aim for controlled movements.

5. Cool-Down: Finish your workout with the specified cool-down stretches. Hold each stretch gently, breathing deeply, to aid in recovery and flexibility.

Form Over Speed: While intensity is key, never sacrifice proper form. Fatigued muscles can lead to compensatory movements and injury. If form starts to break, slightly reduce speed or load to maintain quality.

rows.description_html: Welcome, SmartyGym beginners! Today, we're building a strong cardiovascular foundation with a high-intensity, low-impact Tabata session. Prepare to elevate your heart rate and boost your endurance, setting the stage for future fitness gains.

💪 Main Workout (TABATA)

30 minutes total. Complete blocks A, B, C, then repeat the whole A, B, C sequence, finishing with a final block C. Each block is 8 rounds of 20 sec work / 10 sec rest, alternating its two listed movements for four intervals each. Take an additional 20 sec between blocks: 7 × 4 minutes + 6 × 20 sec = 30 minutes. Use a combined fixed-bar station first, then move once to your dumbbells and floor space.

Block A — controlled upper-body work. These are submaximal intervals, not maximum-repetition tests. Use only movements you already perform confidently.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0685:run}} — 4 intervals; perform 2–4 clean repetitions, then recover for any remaining work time; rise smoothly and lower for 2 sec without swinging; rest 10 sec after each interval.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:3013:low glute bridge on floor}} — 4 intervals; perform 3–5 controlled repetitions, then recover for any remaining work time; lower for 2 sec and rise smoothly, stopping before the shoulders roll forward; rest 10 sec after each interval.

Block B — repeat the familiar pattern with fewer repetitions. Maintain the same technique despite accumulating fatigue.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0685:run}} — 4 intervals; perform 1–3 clean repetitions, then recover for the remaining work time; rise smoothly and lower for 2 sec without swinging; rest 10 sec after each interval.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:3013:low glute bridge on floor}} — 4 intervals; perform 2–4 controlled repetitions, then recover for the remaining work time; lower for 2 sec and rise smoothly through a comfortable range; rest 10 sec after each interval.

Block C — full-body conditioning. Complete this block twice, with the scheduled 20 sec additional recovery between appearances. Keep the dumbbells very light and beside your floor space.

rows.description_html:
This Bodyweight Metabolic workout uses the Tabata format to efficiently elevate your heart rate and boost your metabolism. It's designed for beginners to build foundational cardiovascular endurance without equipment, focusing on consistent effort in short bursts.

The session targets full-body conditioning, aiming for maximum calorie expenditure and improved work capacity in a time-effective manner.
rows.instructions_html: Perform the warm-up as listed. For each Tabata round, complete 20 seconds of the exercise, followed by 10 seconds of rest. Repeat this 8 times for a total of 4 minutes per exercise. Move directly from one Tabata exercise to the next without prolonged breaks in between. For the finisher, complete all listed movements as quickly as possible while maintaining good form. Finish with the cool-down stretches.

  • 10 reps {{exercise:bird-dog:Bird Dog}} — slow and controlled

8 rounds of 20 sec work / 10 sec rest at every station.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0493:Incline Push-Up}} — 8 rounds of 20 sec work / 10 sec rest per station.

rows.name: Ignite Engine
rows.tips_html:
Focus on maintaining a consistent pace during the 20-second work intervals, rather than sprinting the first few and fading. Aim for quality movement over quantity, especially for the Low Impact Burpees.

Listen to your body; if you need extra rest between Tabata exercises, take it, but try to keep it minimal to maintain the metabolic stimulus.

Hydrate well before, during, and after your workout to support your performance and recovery.

For the finisher, feel free to break up the reps for each exercise if you need to, but try to keep moving and minimize rest periods.

This recovery session focuses on active regeneration, combining gentle movement, stretching, and mindful breathing to rejuvenate your body and mind.

It's designed to reduce muscle soreness, improve flexibility, and prepare you for your next training session.

Transition into dynamic mobility exercises, focusing on quality of movement rather than speed.

Proceed to the deep stretching and decompression phase, holding each stretch for the prescribed duration and breathing deeply into the pose.

Utilize a foam roller for targeted myofascial release, applying gentle pressure to release muscle knots and tension.

Conclude with dedicated breathwork and a light cool-down stretch, allowing your body to fully relax and recover.

Listen to your body throughout the session. If you feel any sharp pain, stop the exercise immediately. Prioritize form over load.

Ensure adequate rest between sets to allow for maximal effort on each subsequent set. Prioritize form over weight, especially with compound movements.

Stay hydrated throughout the workout. Have water nearby and take sips between rounds if needed. Listen to your body and take additional rest if you feel overly fatigued. Challenge yourself, but don't push to the point of pain.

Focus on smooth transitions and maintaining effort throughout the entire workout.

Focus on Form Over Speed: Especially on exercises like Burpees and Lunges, maintain good form to prevent injury and ensure you're getting the most out of each rep. Poor form leads to inefficiency and potential setbacks.

rows.instructions_html:

Main Workout (EMOM): At the top of each minute, perform the prescribed number of repetitions for the exercise shown. Use the remaining time in that minute to rest before the next minute begins. The 5th minute is a dedicated rest or active recovery period. Complete 4 rounds total.

Finisher (AMRAP): After a short rest following the main workout, begin the AMRAP. Perform as many rounds and repetitions of the circuit as possible in 10 minutes. Transition quickly between exercises.

Cool Down: Conclude your workout with static stretches, holding each for the recommended duration. Finish with diaphragmatic breathing to lower your heart rate and promote recovery.

rows.name: Trial Ascent
rows.tips_html:
{{exercise:0003:air bike}} This is a long workout. Start at a sustainable pace on the Kettlebell Swings and Goblet Squats, knowing that you have to come back up the ladder. Don't redline too early.

Strategize Breaks: {{exercise:1160:Burpee}}, box jump down with one leg stabilization, {{exercise:1254:band bench press}}, decide on your rep scheme beforehand. Smaller, consistent sets with short breaks are often faster than one big set followed by a long recovery.

Mental Fortitude: The run in the middle is a mental shift. Use it to reset and prepare for the second half of the ladder. Focus on your breathing and staying present.

Scaling: If 20-inch box jump down with one leg stabilization are too high, use a lower box or perform step-ups. Reduce reps on any exercise by 25% if needed to maintain movement quality, but strive to complete the full sequence.

rows.description_html: Welcome, SmartyGym members, to 'The Gauntlet Grind Apex' – an Advanced Bodyweight Challenge designed to test your limits. This AMRAP workout demands relentless effort and mental toughness, pushing your endurance and muscular fortitude to their breaking point. Prepare to face a continuous barrage of compound movements, where consistency and resilience will dictate your success.
rows.instructions_html:
For the Main Workout, set a timer for 20 minutes. Complete the exercises in the listed order, moving from one to the next with minimal rest. Once you complete the 35 Bicycle Crunches, that's one round. Immediately begin the next round, starting again with Burpees. Your score is the total number of rounds and repetitions completed within the 20-minute window.

For the Finisher, begin with a 30-second high plank hold. Then, for each full round you completed in the AMRAP, straddle planche 10 seconds to that base time. Hold your final calculated plank for as long as possible, maintaining strict form.

Maintain proper form throughout all exercises. Hydrate before, during, and after the workout.

rows.description_html: This full-body strength workout focuses on compound movements designed to build a strong foundation. You'll target all major muscle groups with a strategic blend of upper, lower, and core exercises. Prepare to challenge your strength and build resilience.

Main Workout: For each exercise pairing (A1/A2, B1/B2, C1/C2), complete all sets of the first exercise, then all sets of the second, resting as indicated between sets. Choose a challenging weight that allows you to complete the prescribed reps with good form, aiming for 65-80% of your 1RM. Focus intently on the tempo: the first number is the eccentric (lowering) phase in seconds, the second is the pause at the bottom, the third is the concentric (lifting) phase, and the fourth is the pause at the top. E.g., a 3-1-1-0 tempo means 3 seconds down, 1 second pause, 1 second up, no pause at the top.

Finisher: This section is designed for volume completion at a lighter load. Focus on controlled movements and maintaining proper form rather than heavy lifting. Rest only as needed.

Cool-down: Conclude your workout with static stretching to improve flexibility and aid in recovery.

Keep the chest open and pelvis level; use a low lift rather than chasing height. Stop the set if wrists, shoulders or lower back become uncomfortable.

  • 3 sets × 10 reps {{exercise:pilates-neck-pull:Neck Pull}} — alternate sides, 5 reps per side; tempo 3-sec reach, 1-sec pause, 3-sec return; rest 45 sec. Lengthen the moving limbs only as far as you can without changing your rib or pelvic position.

  • 3 sets × 10 reps {{exercise:pilates-jackknife:Jackknife}} — tempo 2-sec gentle pelvic lift, 2-sec pause, 3-sec return; rest 45 sec. Keep knees bent and the movement small; initiate from the lower abdomen without swinging the legs or loading the neck.

rows.main_workout:
🧽 Soft Tissue Preparation 1'

  • Foam roll thighs — 30 sec total; move slowly with light pressure, avoiding knees.

  • Foam roll glutes — 30 sec total; divide time evenly between sides and avoid painful spots.

🔥 Activation 2'

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1167:dynamic chest stretch}} — 1 set; gently open and close the arms at an easy rhythm; rest 10 sec.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1428:wrist circles}} — 1 set; slow, comfortable rotations, changing direction halfway; rest 10 sec.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1363:spine stretch}} — 1 set; ease into a comfortable range and return slowly without holding; rest 10 sec.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:bird-dog:Bird Dog}} — 1 set; very slow, short steps with minimal knee clearance; stay well below fatigue; rest 10 sec.

💪 Main Workout (TABATA)

Complete four 4-minute blocks in this order: A, B, A, C. Each block contains 8 alternating intervals of 20 sec work / 10 sec rest, so each movement receives 4 intervals per block. Take an additional 30 sec recovery after blocks 1, 2 and 4. Total: 16 min intervals + 90 sec recovery = 17 min 30 sec. Keep one light pair of dumbbells beside your floor space.

Block A — alternate these two lines; perform this block twice in the stated schedule.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1459:Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift}} — 4 intervals per A block, 8 total; lower for 2 sec and stand smoothly for 1 sec; keep the weights close and knees softly bent; rest 10 sec after every interval.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1700:Dumbbell Push Press}} — 4 intervals per A block, 8 total; use a shallow knee dip, rise smoothly and lower under control for 2 sec; avoid leaning backward; rest 10 sec after every interval.

Block B — alternate these two lines for 8 intervals.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0293:Dumbbell Bent-over Row}} — 4 intervals; pull smoothly for 1 sec and lower for 2 sec, keeping your trunk still; rest 10 sec after every interval.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0514:Squat Jump}} — 4 intervals; use low jumps, land quietly and reset your balance before each repetition; maintain a smooth, repeatable pace rather than chasing height; rest 10 sec after every interval.

Block C — alternate these two lines for 8 intervals.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1160:Burpee}} — 4 intervals; step back and forward, omit the jump and keep every repetition smooth; finish standing tall without rushing; rest 10 sec after every interval.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1311:Wide Push-Up}} — 4 intervals; position hands only slightly wider than shoulders, lower for 2 sec and rise smoothly for 1 sec; retain 2 clean repetitions in reserve; rest 10 sec after every interval.

⚡ Finisher (For Time)

Set a 5-minute clock and complete 3 rounds of the four movements below: 20 sec work, 5 sec transition, 20 sec rest between rounds. This caps off the session — strong but controlled.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1459:Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift}} — lower for 2 sec and stand smoothly for 1 sec, using the same light weights.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0293:Dumbbell Bent-over Row}} — pull smoothly for 1 sec and lower for 2 sec without rocking.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1160:Burpee}} — continue the step-back, step-forward version without a jump at an even, repeatable pace.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0685:run}} — lift gently for 1 sec and lower for 2 sec, keeping the neck relaxed and range small.

🧘 Cool Down 2'30''

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0613:lying (side) quads stretch}} per side — 1 hold each side; remain still and breathe out into the position; rest 0 sec between sides.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1424:seated glute stretch}} per side — 1 hold each side; remain still without forcing the knee; breathe out into the position; rest 0 sec between sides.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0669:rear deltoid stretch}} per side — 1 hold each side; keep shoulders relaxed and breathe out into the position; rest 0 sec between sides.

Breathe quietly for 30 sec: inhale for approximately 4 sec and exhale for 6 sec, without holding your breath.

rows.main_workout:
🧽 Soft Tissue Preparation 1'

  • Foam roll calves for 30 sec total, 15 sec per side; avoid tender spots and the backs of the knees.

🔥 Activation 3'

  • 30 sec {{exercise:cat-cow-stretch:Cat-cow}} — tempo 3 sec each direction, following your breath; rest 15 sec. Keep the range easy.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:recovery-thoracic-rotation-quadruped:Thoracic Spine Rotation}} — 15 sec per side; tempo 3 sec opening, 3 sec returning; rest 15 sec. Keep the pelvis still.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:pilates-spine-stretch-forward:Spine Stretch Forward}} — tempo 3 sec reaching, 3 sec returning; rest 15 sec. Soften the knees and practise breathing into the back ribs.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:recovery-supine-spinal-twist:Supine Spinal Twist}} — tempo 3 sec easing bent knees sideways, 3 sec returning; alternate sides within a small range; rest 15 sec.

💪 Main Workout (REPS & SETS)

Complete all 3 sets of each exercise before continuing. The prescribed repetitions and rests total 34 min 30 sec: five exercises take 5 min 6 sec each, and two take 4 min 30 sec each. Take the listed rest after every set, including the last; use that final rest to change position. Begin each set with relaxed shoulders and a gentle exhale, never a maximal brace.

  • 3 sets × 12 reps {{exercise:pilates-chest-lift:Chest Lift}} — tempo 2 sec lifting on an exhale, 1 sec pause, 3 sec lowering; rest 30 sec after each set. Cradle the head without pulling and lift only as far as the neck stays comfortable.

  • 3 sets × 12 reps {{exercise:1368:ankle circles}} — alternate sides for 12 total reps, 6 per side; tempo 3 sec extending one leg, 3 sec returning; rest 30 sec after each set. Use the beginner modification with the head resting down and the extending leg high, slightly bent and close to the body; keep the pelvis quiet.

  • 3 sets × 12 reps {{exercise:0130:bench hip extension}} — tempo 3 sec gently rolling upward, 3 sec rolling down; rest 30 sec after each set. Keep both feet grounded and stop before the lower back arches; do not chase height.

  • 3 sets × 10 reps per side {{exercise:pilates-single-leg-circle:Single Leg Circle}} — tempo 3 sec per small complete circle; perform 5 each direction on each side; rest 30 sec after both sides. Keep the supporting knee bent with its foot grounded, soften the moving knee and prevent the pelvis from rocking.

  • 3 sets × 10 reps per side {{exercise:pilates-side-kick-front-back:Side Kick Front and Back}} — tempo 1 sec moving forward, 1 sec moving back, 1 sec returning to centre; rest 30 sec after both sides. One complete sequence is one rep. Support the head, bend the bottom knee and use a short, smooth range without swinging.

  • 3 sets × 12 reps {{exercise:pilates-swimming:Swimming}} — alternate opposite arm-and-leg pairs for 12 total reps, 6 per pair; tempo 2 sec reaching into a low lift, 1 sec pause, 3 sec lowering fully; rest 30 sec after each set. Keep the gaze down, reach long rather than high and reset on the floor between repetitions.

  • 3 sets × 12 reps {{exercise:1167:dynamic chest stretch (male)}} — tempo 3 sec reaching forward on an exhale, 3 sec returning upright on an inhale; rest 30 sec after each set. Keep the knees softly bent and use a comfortable range rather than forcing the fingertips farther.

🧘 Cool Down 3'

  • 45 sec {{exercise:1494:butterfly yoga pose}} — tempo still, relaxed hold; rest 0 sec. Breathe out into the position without pushing the knees downward.

  • 45 sec {{exercise:1511:hamstring stretch}} — tempo still, gentle hold with knees soft; rest 0 sec. Breathe out into the position and avoid forcing the range.

  • 45 sec {{exercise:0690:seated lower back stretch}} — tempo still, comfortable hold; rest 0 sec. Breathe out into the position without pulling or bouncing.

  • 2 min Box breathing — 4 in, 4 hold, 4 out, 4 hold

The Finisher should be completed for time, performing all repetitions as quickly and efficiently as possible.

Remember to maintain proper form throughout the workout to prevent injury and maximize effectiveness. Adjust weights as needed to ensure you can complete each work interval with high intensity.
rows.main_workout:
🧽 Soft Tissue Preparation 1'

  • Foam roll calves — 30 sec total, moving slowly with light pressure.

  • Foam roll upper back — 30 sec, supporting your head and avoiding direct pressure on your neck and lower back.

🔥 Activation 4'

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1167:dynamic chest stretch}} — 1 sets; gently open and close your arms without bouncing; rest 10 sec after each set.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1428:wrist circles}} — 1 sets; make small, comfortable movements, reversing direction halfway; rest 10 sec after each set.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1422:pelvic tilt into bridge}} — 1 sets; lift for 2 sec and lower for 2 sec without arching your back; rest 10 sec after each set.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1368:Ankle Circles}} — 1 sets; move slowly, using one ankle per set; rest 10 sec after each set.

💪 Main Workout (TABATA)

30 minutes total. Complete seven 4-minute blocks: run the A, B, C, C sequence, then repeat blocks A, B and C once more. Each block contains 8 rounds of 20 sec work / 10 sec rest, alternating its two listed lines. Take an additional 20 sec between blocks. Total: 7 × 4 min + 6 × 20 sec = 30 min. Use one combined bodyweight support station with adjacent clear floor space. These are controlled intervals, not maximal-effort tests.

Block A — controlled upper-body strength. Alternate the following two lines for 8 intervals total. Use light foot support on a secure, fixed platform when necessary to preserve two repetitions in reserve.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0279:decline push-up}} — 4 intervals; lift smoothly for about 2 sec and lower for 3 sec, without swinging; rest 10 sec after each interval. Stop repetitions early if your next repetition would require momentum.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0806:suspended push-up}} — 4 intervals; lower for 3 sec and rise smoothly for 2 sec; rest 10 sec after each interval. Keep shoulders controlled and use only a comfortable depth, with upper arms no deeper than approximately parallel to the floor.

Block B — repeatable strength. Alternate the following two lines for 8 intervals total. Retain the same assistance and range; match Block A's clean repetitions rather than chasing fatigue.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1014:band v-up}} — 4 intervals; lift for about 2 sec and lower for 3 sec, maintaining a quiet trunk; rest 10 sec after each interval. Increase foot assistance if needed to keep two repetitions in reserve.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0806:suspended push-up}} — 4 intervals; lower for 3 sec and rise for 2 sec through the same comfortable range; rest 10 sec after each interval. Keep your neck relaxed and stop before shoulder position changes.

Blocks C and D — conditioning and trunk control. Perform the following pair as one 8-interval block, take the scheduled 20 sec recovery, then repeat the block once. Move to the adjacent floor area and remain there for the rest of the session.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0501:jack burpee}} — 4 intervals per block, 2 blocks; use the low-impact version: step back and forward, then step feet out and in instead of jumping; rest 10 sec after each interval. Move at a smooth, repeatable pace without an additional arm-lowering repetition.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0508:janda sit-up}} — 4 intervals per block, 2 blocks; keep feet planted, gently draw heels toward you, rise for 2 sec and lower for 3 sec; rest 10 sec after each interval. Use a shorter range if necessary and never pull on your neck.

⚡ Finisher (5 minutes)

Set a 5-minute clock and complete 3 clean rounds of the movements below. This caps off the session — keep the pace strong but controlled and stop the clock at 5 minutes.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0501:jack burpee}}

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0508:janda sit-up}}

🧘 Cool Down 3'

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0613:lying (side) quads stretch}} — 1 hold per side; remain still with knees comfortably aligned, breathe out into the position, then allow 10 sec to change position.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1424:seated glute stretch}} — 1 hold per side; hold without bouncing or forcing the knee, breathe out into the position, then allow 10 sec to change position.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:1346:kneeling lat stretch}} — 2 gentle holds; remain still and breathe out into the position, allowing 10 sec total between holds and for repositioning.

Breathe comfortably for 30 sec: inhale for approximately 4 sec and exhale for approximately 6 sec, without holding your breath.

rows.description_html: Today we test your endurance and mental grit with a challenging Tabata workout. This format will push your limits, demanding maximum effort in short bursts followed by brief recovery periods. Prepare to feel the burn and build unwavering stamina.

Cool Down: Focus on static stretches to improve flexibility and aid muscle recovery. Conclude with diaphragmatic breathing to down-regulate your nervous system and promote relaxation.

Focus on maintaining good form and moving efficiently through each exercise to complete the challenge as quickly as possible.
rows.instructions_html:

Record your total time to track progress in future sessions. Prioritize correct form over speed, especially as you begin.

rows.name: Velocity Surge Challenge
rows.tips_html:
For Kettlebell Swings, focus on a powerful hip drive, not arm strength. The bell should not go higher than shoulder height.

If Burpees are too challenging, perform a Half-Burpee: hands to floor, step feet back, step feet forward, stand up.

Keep your core engaged throughout all movements to protect your back and enhance power.

Hydrate well before, during, and after your workout.

rows.description_html:
A 25-minute METABOLIC EMOM (Every Minute on the Minute) for time-pressed adults who want a real conditioning effect without equipment. Each minute you perform a prescribed work bout, then rest with the remaining seconds. The workout finishes with a short Finisher and a structured Cool Down so you leave loose, not wrecked.

This session is designed by Coach Haris Falas as part of the SmartyGym 84-day periodization. It targets aerobic capacity, full-body coordination, and repeat-effort tolerance.
rows.instructions_html:
How to run this EMOM:

  • Start a clock for 25 minutes.

  • At the top of every minute (0:00, 1:00, 2:00…) perform the prescribed reps of the listed exercise, rotating through the four movements.

  • Once you finish your reps, the rest of that minute is your rest. Aim to leave at least 10–15 seconds of rest before the next minute starts.

  • If you cannot finish a minute with rest, reduce the reps by 20–30% for the rest of the workout. Quality over quantity.

  • After the EMOM, perform the Finisher straight through For Time, then complete the Cool Down without rushing.

Suggested rep targets (Intermediate, 3★):

  • Burpees: 8–10 reps

  • Mountain Climbers: 30 reps (15 per side)

  • Jump Squats: 12–15 reps

  • Decline Push-ups: 8–10 reps

rows.name: Cadence Complex
rows.tips_html:
• Pace from minute 1. EMOMs are won by athletes who control intensity early. If you sprint round 1, you will collapse by round 4.

  • Breathe in a steady rhythm. Nasal inhale, mouth exhale on the effort. Avoid breath-holding on push-ups and squats.

  • Land softly on jumping reps. Knees track over toes, hips back, full foot contact. This protects your joints during repeated impact.

  • Scale, do not skip. Replace decline push-ups with floor push-ups, jump squats with bodyweight squats, and burpees with step-back burpees if needed.

  • Do not skip the cool down. The 🧘 Cool Down section is what lets you train again tomorrow without stiffness.

rows.description_html:
Dominate your lower body with this advanced, bodyweight-focused strength builder. This session targets every major muscle group in your legs and glutes through highly effective reps and sets, pushing your muscular endurance and strength.

Prepare for a challenging workout designed to forge a powerful foundation from the ground up, utilizing only your bodyweight for maximal gains.
rows.instructions_html:

Rest fully between sets to allow for maximum effort on each subsequent set. For bodyweight exercises, focus on deep range of motion and muscle contraction.

The Finisher is designed for volume completion with lighter intensity. Maintain good form throughout, but aim for controlled repetitions to fatigue the muscles. Conclude with the Cool Down, holding each stretch for the recommended duration and finishing with diaphragmatic breathing to aid recovery.

rows.tips_html:
• Quality over quantity: For bodyweight exercises, execute each rep with perfect form, focusing on the muscle contraction rather than just completing the movement.

• Mind-muscle connection: Actively think about the muscles you are working. This enhances recruitment and makes bodyweight exercises more effective.

rows.description_html:
This intermediate bodyweight strength workout is designed to build a strong and resilient upper body. Focus on controlled movements and activating each muscle group through the full range of motion.

You'll alternate between pressing and pulling movements to ensure balanced development, culminating in a challenging finisher to solidify your gains.
rows.instructions_html:
1. Warm-Up: Begin with the prescribed warm-up exercises to prepare your body for movement. Focus on controlled, deliberate movements to increase blood flow and range of motion.

2. Main Workout - Circuit 1: Perform all exercises in Circuit 1 back-to-back with minimal rest between exercises. Once you've completed one round of all four exercises, rest for 60 seconds. Repeat this circuit for a total of 3 rounds.

3. Main Workout - Circuit 2: After completing Circuit 1, move on to Circuit 2. Follow the same structure: perform all exercises back-to-back, rest for 60 seconds after each round, and complete 3 total rounds.

4. Tempo: Pay attention to the tempo listed (e.g., 2010). This means 2 seconds on the eccentric (lowering) phase, 0-second pause at the bottom, 1 second on the concentric (lifting) phase, and 0-second pause at the top. Adjust the tempo to your fitness level, but aim for controlled movements.

5. Cool-Down: Finish your workout with the specified cool-down stretches. Hold each stretch gently, breathing deeply, to aid in recovery and flexibility.

rows.instructions_html:
This advanced lower body strength workout is designed to push your limits. For all exercises, select a weight that allows you to complete the prescribed repetitions with good form, but challenges you significantly in the last 1-2 reps.

Maintain a controlled tempo: generally, a 3-second eccentric (lowering) phase, a 1-second pause at the bottom, and an explosive 1-2 second concentric (lifting) phase. This maximizes time under tension and muscle recruitment.

Prioritize form over load. If your form breaks down, reduce the weight. Track your weights to ensure progressive overload each week. Aim to increase the load or reps when you can comfortably complete all sets and reps with perfect technique.

Focus on maintaining good form and a consistent pace throughout to maximize your effort and results. This workout is perfect for those looking to improve their cardiovascular fitness and boost fat loss.
rows.instructions_html:

Rest only as needed to maintain good form. For the Finisher, complete the prescribed repetitions for each exercise as fast as possible. Finally, perform the cool-down stretches to aid recovery.

rows.description_html: This equipment-focused workout is designed for intermediate SmartyGym members ready to test their limits under pressure. Adjust weights as needed to ensure good form for all reps within the minute.

Forge a solid upper body foundation with this beginner-friendly strength session. Focus on controlled movements and proper form to build foundational strength in your chest, back, and arms.

This workout emphasizes quality over speed, setting you up for consistent progress in your strength journey.
rows.instructions_html:
Select weights that allow you to complete all prescribed repetitions with good form. For compound movements like Bench Press and Seated Row, aim for 90 seconds of rest between sets. For isolation exercises, rest for 60 seconds between sets.

Focus on a controlled tempo: lower the weight for 3 seconds, pause briefly at the bottom, then lift for 1-2 seconds. Prioritize muscle activation over lifting heavy.

Record the weights you use to ensure you can progressively add load in future sessions.

Immediately calculate your Squat Jump target (AMRAP rounds x 3). Rest 3 minutes after the AMRAP, then begin the 10-minute EMOM. Focus on hitting your reps at the start of each minute, then recover for the remainder. Ensure controlled movements, especially as fatigue sets in.

{{exercise:0003:air bike}} In the AMRAP, find a sustainable pace that allows you to maintain movement quality. Don't go out too fast and burn out before the EMOM.

rows.description_html: This beginner-friendly, bodyweight AMRAP workout focuses on continuous movement to maximize caloric expenditure and build foundational cardiovascular fitness. Get ready to sweat and boost your metabolism with dynamic exercises that challenge your entire body.
rows.instructions_html: Perform the workout as an AMRAP (As Many Rounds As Possible) for the designated time. Complete all reps for each exercise in a round before moving to the next. Focus on maintaining good form throughout, especially as you fatigue. Rest as needed, but try to keep your break periods brief to maximize your calorie burn. If an exercise becomes too challenging, modify it or take a short break antes resuming.
rows.main_workout:
🧽 Soft Tissue Preparation 1'

  • Self-massage — 30 sec total across both thighs using your palms; apply gentle pressure and avoid the knees.

  • Self-massage — 30 sec total across both calves while seated on the floor; use slow hand strokes without digging into tender areas.

🔥 Activation 3'

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1167:dynamic chest stretch}} — 1 set; gently open and close your arms at a relaxed pace; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1428:wrist circles}} — 1 set; move slowly through comfortable ranges, changing direction halfway; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1368:Ankle Circles}} — 1 set; seated on the floor, alternate ankles with small, unhurried movements; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1422:pelvic tilt into bridge}} — 1 set; gently lift and lower with easy breathing, without tiring the muscles; rest 15 sec.

💪 Main Workout (AMRAP)

Time cap: 26 min. Repeat the six movements in order for as many comfortable rounds as possible, keeping every recovery period. Each station uses 30 sec for the prescribed repetitions followed by 60 sec rest, including transitions. One full round takes 9 min: complete two rounds, then continue through the remaining 8 min. Stop at the cap; do not add a final recovery beyond it.

  • 10 reps {{exercise:0514:jump squat}} — per round, over 30 sec; lower for 2 sec and stand for 1 sec at a smooth, repeatable pace. Use a comfortable depth and keep heels grounded; rest 60 sec.

  • 10 reps {{exercise:1326:chin-up}} — per round, over 30 sec; draw elbows back for 1 sec and return for 2 sec, gently engaging your upper back without an anchor or implement. Keep shoulders relaxed and movement smooth; rest 60 sec.

  • 10 reps {{exercise:3211:Kneeling Push-Up}} — per round, over 30 sec; lower for 2 sec and return for 1 sec at a smooth, repeatable pace. Keep knees grounded and shorten the depth as needed to retain 2 good repetitions in reserve; rest 60 sec.

  • 10 reps {{exercise:0685:run}} — per round, over 30 sec; lift for 1 sec and lower for 2 sec at a smooth, repeatable pace. Keep ribs relaxed and finish with the hips rather than arching the back; rest 60 sec.

  • 10 reps {{exercise:0630:Mountain Climber}} — per round, over 30 sec; alternate 5 controlled knee movements per side, taking 3 sec to bring each knee forward and return. Keep hips steady, use short steps and never hop; rest 60 sec.

  • 10 reps {{exercise:2466:bridge - mountain climber (cross body)}} — per round, over 30 sec; alternate 5 repetitions per side, taking 3 sec to extend and return smoothly. Keep the range short enough that your lower back stays comfortable; rest 60 sec.

⚡ Finisher (5 minutes)

Set a 5-minute clock and complete 3 clean rounds of the movements below. This caps off the session — keep the pace strong but controlled and stop the clock at 5 minutes.

  • 10 reps {{exercise:1685:squat to overhead reach}}

  • 30 sec {{exercise:3360:Bear Crawl}}

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1160:Burpee}}

🧘 Cool Down 3'

  • 30 sec per side {{exercise:0669:rear deltoid stretch}} — 1 set; hold gently without bouncing and breathe out into the position; rest 0 sec between sides.

  • 30 sec per side {{exercise:0613:lying (side) quads stretch}} — 1 set; keep the knees comfortably aligned, hold still and breathe out into the position; rest 0 sec between sides.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1494:butterfly yoga pose}} — 1 set; sit comfortably without forcing the knees downward, hold still and breathe out into the position; rest 0 sec.

  • 2 min Box breathing — 4 in, 4 hold, 4 out, 4 hold
rows.name: Ember Step Ladder
rows.tips_html:
Pacing is Key: For an AMRAP, start at a sustainable pace you can maintain for the full 20 minutes. It's better to keep moving consistently than to go all-out and burn out quickly.

Listen to Your Body: As a beginner, it's crucial to pay attention to your body. If you feel any sharp pain, stop the exercise immediately. Soreness is normal, but pain is a warning sign.

Controlled Breathing: Focus on deep, controlled breathing throughout the workout. Inhale through your nose and exhale through your mouth. This helps oxygenate your muscles and manage fatigue.

Modification for Push-ups: If full push-ups are too difficult, perform them with your knees on the ground. As you get stronger, try progressing to full push-ups.

rows.name: Metabolic Torchflow
rows.tips_html:
Maintain a steady, aggressive pace throughout the working portion of each minute to maximize calorie expenditure. Push hard on the cardio machines to hit your calorie target quickly.

Focus on controlled breathing to manage your heart rate and sustain the intensity. Inhale through your nose, exhale powerfully through your mouth.

Prioritize form, especially on kettlebell swings and burpee box jumps, to prevent injury and ensure effective muscle activation. If your form falters, reduce speed or reps slightly.

Don't be afraid to modify if needed, but challenge yourself. This workout is designed to be tough, so embrace the burn and push past your comfort zone.

rows.description_html: This Circuit Challenge is designed to push your bodyweight capabilities to the brink. It's a relentless test of endurance, strength, and mental fortitude. There's no room for easing up – the clock is running, and every rep counts.
rows.instructions_html:
After your warm-up, begin the main workout. Complete all exercises in the circuit consecutively with minimal rest between them.

Once you finish one round of all five exercises, immediately begin the next round. Your goal is to complete all 5 rounds as fast as possible. Record your total time.

For the Finisher, hold a plank for 30 seconds. Rest for 15 seconds. Then, increase the plank hold time by 10 seconds for each subsequent round (e.g., 40s, 50s, 60s...) until you can no longer hold the plank with good form.

rows.tips_html:
Pacing is critical for the main workout. The burpees and jump squats will quickly elevate your heart rate, so find a sustainable rhythm from the start.

Break up your reps strategically if needed, especially for the burpees and push-ups. Short, planned breaks are better than longer, unplanned ones.

Experience the Cadence Blast, an advanced bodyweight Tabata workout designed to ignite your metabolism and incinerate calories. This high-intensity session will push your limits, combining explosive movements with strategic pauses to maximize your fat-burning potential and improve cardiovascular endurance.

Prepare for a relentless challenge that will leave you feeling accomplished and energized, proving your body is the ultimate calorie-burning machine.
rows.instructions_html:
Tabata protocol: each exercise is 8 rounds of 20 seconds maximum effort followed by 10 seconds rest, totalling 4 minutes per exercise. Move directly to the next exercise without extra rest. Push hard during every 20-second work interval — quality first, then intensity.

How to run this workout: begin with the soft tissue prep and activation exactly as listed. Move into the main Tabata block performing each exercise for one full 4-minute Tabata before moving to the next. Use the finisher to empty the tank, then complete the cool down without skipping it.

rows.tips_html:
Maximize Tabata Intervals: During the 20-second work periods, focus on explosive, high-quality movements. The goal is maximum effort, not just continuous motion.

Swift Transitions: With only 10 seconds of rest between intervals and 30 seconds between Tabata blocks, efficiency is key. Prepare mentally and physically for the next exercise to avoid wasting precious time.

Listen to Your Body: While this is an advanced workout, proper form is paramount. If you feel your form breaking down, take a slightly longer pause before resuming with better technique. Quality trumps quantity to prevent injury.

Hydration and Recovery: Replenish your fluids throughout the workout and ensure adequate post-workout nutrition to support muscle recovery and energy restoration. This will help you bounce back stronger for your next session.

rows.description_html:
A 25-minute METABOLIC EMOM (Every Minute on the Minute) using simple equipment — dumbbells or kettlebells — to build full-body conditioning, posterior-chain power, and repeat-effort capacity. Designed for adults who want a complete training stimulus in under half an hour.

This session is part of the SmartyGym 84-day periodization by Coach Haris Falas. It pairs a strength-biased pull/push movement with a hinge and a metabolic accelerator so you train every major pattern in one block.
rows.instructions_html:
How to run this EMOM:

  • Start a clock for 25 minutes.

  • At the top of every minute (0:00, 1:00, 2:00…) perform the prescribed reps of the listed movement, rotating through the four exercises in order.

  • Aim to finish each minute with at least 15 seconds of rest. That rest is the engine of the workout — protect it.

  • If you cannot finish in time, drop the load or the reps for the remainder of the workout. Do not chase failure.

  • After the EMOM, perform the Finisher straight through For Time, then complete the full Cool Down.

Suggested loading and reps (Intermediate, 4★):

  • Dumbbell Thrusters: 8–10 reps with a moderate pair (women ~2×8 kg, men ~2×12 kg).

  • Kettlebell Swings: 15 reps Russian style (women ~12 kg, men ~16–20 kg).

  • Renegade Rows: 8 reps total, alternating sides.

  • Goblet Squats: 12 reps with a controlled tempo.
rows.main_workout:
🧽 Soft Tissue Preparation 2'

  • Foam roll thighs — 30 sec total, moving slowly with comfortable contact.

  • Foam roll glutes — 30 sec total, dividing time evenly between sides.

  • Foam roll calves — 30 sec total, avoiding direct contact over joints.

  • Foam roll upper back — 30 sec, supporting your head and avoiding the neck and lower back.

🔥 Activation 3'

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1167:dynamic chest stretch}} — 1 set; open and return gently over 3 sec; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1428:wrist circles}} — 1 set; make small, comfortable rotations, changing direction halfway; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1363:spine stretch}} — 1 set; gently reach forward from the hips and return over 5 sec, without forcing range; rest 15 sec.

  • 8 reps {{exercise:bird-dog:Bird Dog}} — 1 set; ease the hips backward and return slowly over 5 sec, keeping the shoulders comfortable; rest 15 sec.

💪 Main Workout (EMOM)

30 minutes: 5 rounds of the following 6-minute sequence. Repeat Minutes 1–6 five times. Each minute contains 40 sec of work and 20 sec of rest, including transitions. Use moderate loads and finish each resistance interval with 1–2 technically sound reps available. Keep the kettlebells beside one clear floor area.

  • Minute 1: 40 sec {{exercise:0549:Kettlebell Swing}} — 3 sets total; use a crisp hip extension and controlled return, letting the bell float no higher than chest height; rest 20 sec.

  • Minute 2: 40 sec {{exercise:0550:Kettlebell Thruster}} — 3 sets total; hold one bell with both hands, lower over 2 sec and rise into a smooth overhead finish without leaning backward; rest 20 sec.

  • Minute 3: 40 sec {{exercise:1345:Kettlebell Row}} — 3 sets total; draw both bells upward over 1 sec and lower over 2 sec, maintaining a steady torso; rest 20 sec.

  • Minute 4: 40 sec {{exercise:3360:Bear Crawl}} — 3 sets total; take slow, short steps forward and backward within a small area, keeping knees low and hips quiet; rest 20 sec.

  • Minute 5: 40 sec {{exercise:0267:crunch (hands overhead)}} — 3 sets total; lift over 1 sec and lower over 2 sec through a small controlled range, without pulling the head forward; rest 20 sec.

  • Minute 6: 40 sec {{exercise:0687:russian twist}} — 3 sets total; keep feet grounded and turn gently from side to side over 2 sec per side, without rounding or forcing rotation; rest 20 sec.

⚡ Finisher (5 minutes)

Set a 5-minute clock and complete 3 clean rounds of the movements below. This caps off the session — keep the pace strong but controlled and stop the clock at 5 minutes.

  • 40 sec {{exercise:0549:Kettlebell Swing}}

  • 40 sec {{exercise:0550:Kettlebell Thruster}}

  • 40 sec {{exercise:1345:Kettlebell Row}}

  • 40 sec {{exercise:3360:Bear Crawl}}

🧘 Cool Down 3'

💪 Main Workout (REPS & SETS)

Complete straight sets in the listed order; do not alternate exercises. Use dumbbells and one adjustable bench. Keep 2 reps in reserve throughout. The prescribed work and recovery budget is approximately 40 minutes; use the recovery after each final set to change position and adjust the bench.

  • 5 sets × 4 reps {{exercise:1459:Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift}} — tempo 2-sec lower, 1-sec pause, lift with explosive intent over approximately 1 sec, 1-sec reset; rest 150 sec. Keep knees softly bent, weights close and your spine steady; stop descending before your back position changes.

  • 4 sets × 4 reps {{exercise:0289:dumbbell bench press}} — tempo 2-sec lower, 1-sec pause, lift with explosive intent over approximately 1 sec, 1-sec reset; rest 120 sec. Keep ribs stacked over your pelvis and avoid leaning backward.

  • 4 sets × 4 reps {{exercise:0314:Dumbbell Incline Press}} — tempo 2-sec lower, 1-sec pause, lift with explosive intent over approximately 1 sec, 1-sec reset; rest 120 sec. Set the bench at 30–45 degrees, plant your feet and keep your shoulders supported.

  • 2 sets × 5 reps {{exercise:0361:dumbbell one arm shoulder press}} — tempo 2-sec lower, 1-sec pause, lift with explosive intent over approximately 1 sec, 1-sec reset; rest 120 sec. Flatten the bench and keep elbows comfortably near your sides.

  • 1 set × 6 reps {{exercise:0293:dumbbell bent over row}} — tempo 2-sec lower, 1-sec pause, smooth 1-sec extension, 1-sec reset; rest 120 sec. Return the bench to a comfortable incline; use a moderate load and keep upper arms steady.

⚡ Finisher (REPS & SETS)

Approximately 5 minutes. These are three controlled accessory sets, not a circuit or conditioning test. Stay at the same incline bench, use lighter dumbbells and retain 2 clean reps in reserve. Reduce the load for the final exercise as needed to accommodate the additional repetitions.

  • 1 set × 8 reps {{exercise:0319:dumbbell incline fly}} — tempo 2-sec lower, 1-sec comfortable pause, smooth 1-sec return, 1-sec reset; rest 60 sec. Maintain softly bent elbows and stop before the shoulders feel strained.

  • 1 set × 8 reps {{exercise:0328:dumbbell incline shoulder raise}} — tempo 2-sec return, 1-sec pause, smooth 1-sec reach, 1-sec reset; rest 60 sec. Keep elbows straight without locking; use a small shoulder-blade movement rather than bending the arms.

  • 1 set × 8 reps {{exercise:0293:dumbbell bent over row}} — tempo 2-sec lower, 1-sec pause, smooth 1-sec extension, 1-sec reset; rest 60 sec. Keep the movement comfortable at the elbows and finish without grinding.

🧘 Cool Down 4'

  • 1 set × 30 sec each side {{exercise:1271:chest and front of shoulder stretch}} — hold still at mild tension and breathe out into the position; rest 5 sec between sides.

  • 1 set × 30 sec each side {{exercise:1511:hamstring stretch}} — hold still without rounding forcefully or bouncing; rest 5 sec between sides.

  • 1 set × 30 sec each side {{exercise:1424:seated glute stretch}} — hold still and breathe out into the position; rest 5 sec between sides.

  • 2 min Box breathing — 4 in, 4 hold, 4 out, 4 hold
rows.name: Keystone Press
rows.tips_html:
Maintain a neutral spine during all deadlift variations; imagine a straight line from your head to your hips. Engage your core to protect your back.

Control the eccentric (lowering) phase of your presses to maximize muscle recruitment and minimize injury risk. Aim for a 2-3 second lower.

For lunges, ensure your front knee tracks over your toes and your back knee gently lowers towards the ground. Keep your torso upright.

rows.description_html: This advanced EMOM cardio workout features a relentless sequence of bodyweight exercises designed to sustain a high heart rate and build explosive cardiovascular endurance while weaving through fundamental movement patterns.
rows.instructions_html: Perform this workout as an EMOM (Every Minute On the Minute). Start a timer and complete the prescribed repetitions for the scheduled exercise within that minute. Use any remaining time in the minute to rest before the next exercise begins at the top of the next minute. Maintain high intensity throughout the main workout and finisher.
rows.main_workout:
🧽 Soft Tissue Preparation 1'

  • Self-massage — 30 sec total across both calves using gentle hand pressure; avoid tender spots and the backs of the knees.

  • Self-massage — 30 sec total across the fronts of both thighs using broad palm pressure; keep the sensation comfortable.

🔥 Activation 3'

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1422:pelvic tilt into bridge}} — 1 set; lift and lower gently over about 3 sec per repetition; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1368:Ankle Circles}} — 1 set, 15 sec per side; use slow, comfortable rotations; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:0257:circles knee stretch}} — 1 set; make small, unforced movements with soft knees; rest 15 sec.

  • 30 sec {{exercise:1428:wrist circles}} — 1 set; move gently in both directions without forcing range; rest 15 sec.

💪 Main Workout (EMOM)

30 minutes total: repeat the six-minute sequence for 5 rounds. Begin each station at the start of its minute, work for 35 sec and rest for 25 sec. Repeated stations are intentional: maintain the same comfortable cadence rather than increasing speed. Standing work stays together, followed by floor work in the same clear training area.

  • Minute 1: 35 sec {{exercise:0501:jack burpee}} — 3 sets across the block; alternate sides with short steps and comfortable knee height; use a smooth, repeatable pace and rest 25 sec.

  • Minute 2: 35 sec {{exercise:3636:high knee against wall}} — 3 sets across the block; maintain the previous cadence with shallow, comfortable knee bends; use a smooth, repeatable pace and rest 25 sec.

  • Minute 3: 35 sec {{exercise:butt-kicks-cardio:Butt Kicks}} — 3 sets across the block; place each foot quietly and keep the front knee aligned with the toes; use a smooth, repeatable pace and rest 25 sec.

  • Minute 4: 35 sec {{exercise:high-knees:High Knees}} — 3 sets across the block; keep the torso upright and avoid pushing for additional depth; use a smooth, repeatable pace and rest 25 sec.

  • Minute 5: 35 sec {{exercise:3224:jack jump (male)}} — 3 sets across the block; take very small forward and backward steps within your floor space, keeping hips steady; use a smooth, repeatable pace and rest 25 sec.

  • Minute 6: 35 sec {{exercise:3224:jack jump (male)}} — 3 sets across the block; repeat without speeding up, keeping the neck relaxed and breathing continuously; use a smooth, repeatable pace and rest 25 sec.

⚡ Finisher (5 minutes)

Set a 5-minute clock and complete 3 clean rounds of the movements below. This caps off the session — keep the pace strong but controlled and stop the clock at 5 minutes.

  • 40 sec {{exercise:0501:jack burpee}}

  • 40 sec {{exercise:3224:jack jump (male)}}

🧘 Cool Down 3'

  • 40 sec {{exercise:1390:seated calf stretch}} — 1 set; hold gently without bouncing and breathe out into the position; rest 0 sec before transitioning.

  • 40 sec {{exercise:0613:lying (side) quads stretch}} — 1 set, 20 sec per side; hold a mild, steady position and breathe out slowly; rest 0 sec before transitioning.

  • 40 sec {{exercise:0669:rear deltoid stretch}} — 1 set, 20 sec per side; keep the shoulder relaxed and hold without bouncing; rest 0 sec before the breathing period.

  • 2 min Box breathing — 4 in, 4 hold, 4 out, 4 hold
rows.name: Cadence Current Weave
rows.tips_html:
Focus on powerful, controlled movements rather than just speed. Quality over quantity.

If you find yourself consistently unable to complete the reps within the minute, slightly reduce the target reps for the following round or work on improving your power output.

Stay hydrated throughout the workout and listen to your body. Modify as needed, but always push for intensity.

rows.description_html: This workout is a true test of endurance and functional strength, designed to push your limits in a high-intensity circuit format. Expect a relentless pace, demanding both physical and mental resilience. Prepare to drive through fatigue and emerge stronger on the other side.
rows.instructions_html: Complete the warm-up as listed. For the main workout, perform all five exercises consecutively with minimal rest in between. Once you complete all exercises, rest for 90-120 seconds before starting the next round. Complete a total of 5 rounds. For the finisher, continuously push the sled for 5 minutes, aiming for maximum distance or pushes. Conclude with the cool-down stretches.
rows.main_workout:
🧽 Soft Tissue Preparation

  • 60 sec Foam roll quadriceps — slow controlled passes

  • 60 sec Foam roll thoracic spine — pause on tender spots

  • 45 sec Lacrosse ball glute release — each side

🔥 Activation 5'

  • 10 reps {{exercise:3021:scapula push-up}} — slow and controlled

  • 10 reps {{exercise:fire-hydrant:Fire Hydrant}} — slow and controlled

  • 10 reps {{exercise:clamshell:Clamshell}} — slow and controlled

  • 10 reps {{exercise:bird-dog:Bird Dog}} — slow and controlled

💪 Main Workout (CIRCUIT)

6 rounds. Rest 60 sec between rounds.

  • 45 sec {{exercise:0514:jump squat}}

  • 45 sec {{exercise:1326:chin-up}}

  • 45 sec {{exercise:bw-crab-walk:Crab Walk}}

  • 45 sec {{exercise:1472:forward jump}}

  • 45 sec {{exercise:0501:jack burpee}}

⚡ Finisher (For Time)

2 rounds for time. Move well, keep breathing, stop if form breaks.

  • 12 reps {{exercise:1476:one leg squat}}

  • 12 reps {{exercise:1772:elbow lift - reverse push-up}}

  • 12 reps {{exercise:3360:Bear Crawl}}

🧘 Cool Down

  • 45 sec {{exercise:1364:standing pelvic tilt}} — breathe out into the position

  • 45 sec {{exercise:cat-cow-stretch:Cat-cow}} — breathe out into the position

  • 45 sec {{exercise:2329:Spine Twist}} — breathe out into the position

  • 60 sec Box breathing — 4 in, 4 hold, 4 out, 4 hold
rows.name: Gauntlet Drive
rows.tips_html:
Pacing is crucial for this workout. Maintain a steady, sustainable tempo throughout the main circuit to avoid burning out in early rounds.

Focus on controlled breathing. Inhale deeply before each rep and exhale with effort to manage your heart rate and oxygen intake.

Break up your reps strategically on the Wall Balls and Thrusters if needed, but try to keep transitions between exercises swift.

For beginner modification, reduce the number of rounds to 3-4, lower the intensity/weight, or decrease rep counts by 3-5 reps per exercise.

rows.description_html: This metabolic workout focuses on bodyweight movements to elevate your heart rate and build functional strength. Axial Current uses the Tabata protocol to maximize your effort in short, intense bursts, followed by brief recovery periods, making it ideal for beginners.
rows.instructions_html: Perform the soft tissue preparation as listed. Move into the activation exercises to prepare your body for movement. For the main workout, complete each Tabata exercise for 20 seconds of work followed by 10 seconds of rest, for 8 rounds, before moving to the next exercise. Rest for 60-90 seconds between each Tabata exercise. The finisher is "for time", meaning complete the listed repetitions as fast as possible with good form. Finish with the cool down stretches to aid recovery.
rows.main_workout:

  • 60 sec Foam roll quadriceps — slow controlled passes

  • 10 reps {{exercise:cat-cow-stretch:Cat-cow}} — slow and controlled

8 rounds of 20 sec work / 10 sec rest at every station.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0493:Incline Push-Up}} — 8 rounds of 20 sec work / 10 sec rest per station.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:bird-dog:Bird Dog}} — 8 rounds of 20 sec work / 10 sec rest per station.

  • 20 sec {{exercise:0662:Push-Up}} — 8 rounds of 20 sec work / 10 sec rest per station.

⚡ Finisher (For Time)

3 rounds for time. Move well, keep breathing, stop if form breaks.

rows.name: Axial Current
rows.tips_html:
Focus on maintaining good form throughout each exercise, even as you get tired. Quality over quantity is key for beginners.

Listen to your body. If you need more rest than prescribed, take it. This is a beginner workout, and gradual progression is important.

Stay hydrated! Drink water before, during, and after your workout.
